title: Il tient à vous  (He Cares About You)

segments.t: Recovering at home after a traumatic accident, assistant Noemie welcomes Mathias Barneville and his wife Catherine into her apartment. While Mathias tries to minimize the awkwardness, Catherine directly brings up Noemie's career plans and reveals Mathias's true devotion. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Je vous pose ce sac sur la table.
Merci Mathias, c'est très gentil à vous.
Voulez-vous manger une bonne soupe chaude, Noémie?
Non merci Catherine, ne vous embêtez pas.
Nous allons te laisser te reposer maintenant.
Je ne suis pas paralysée non plus!
Mathias m'a tout raconté aux urgences.
Qu'est-ce qu'il vous a raconté exactement?
Vous voulez vraiment quitter l'agence ASK?
Un chasseur de têtes m'a contactée.
Noémie est très demandée pour son talent.
Ce n'est peut-être pas le bon moment.
Je vais réfléchir à toute cette situation.
Mathias tient énormément à vous, Noémie.
Let's see how Catherine gently challenges Noemie while revealing the profound loyalty of Mathias.
Je vous pose ce sac sur la table.
'I put this bag on the table for you.' A considerate announcement setting down groceries. Notice how 'place' leads directly into the noun meaning 'bag'.
Merci Mathias, c'est très gentil à vous.

'Thank you Mathias, that is very kind of you.' A polite acknowledgment expressing domestic gratitude. Notice how the short vowel drops before a vowel sound around 'it is', making the phrase flow smoothly as one unit.
Voulez-vous manger une bonne soupe chaude, Noémie?
'Do you want to eat a good hot soup, Noemie?' The adjective meaning 'good' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
Non merci Catherine, ne vous embêtez pas.

'No thank you Catherine, do not trouble yourself.' The two-part French negation brackets the verb for 'trouble' on both sides. The two-part French negation brackets the verb for 'trouble' on both sides.
Nous allons te laisser te reposer maintenant.

'We are going to let you rest now.' French forms the near future by pairing the present tense of 'to go' directly with 'to rest'. French forms the near future by pairing the present tense of 'to go' directly with 'to rest'.
Je ne suis pas paralysée non plus!

'I am not paralyzed either!' This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past verb form for 'paralyzed'. This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past verb form for 'paralyzed'.
Mathias m'a tout raconté aux urgences.
'Mathias told me everything at the emergency room.' A candid disclosure revealing hospital confidences. Notice how 'has' leads directly into the noun meaning 'emergency room'.
Qu'est-ce qu'il vous a raconté exactement?
'What did he tell you exactly?' The standard spoken question formula at the front turns the statement about 'has' into a natural inquiry.
Vous voulez vraiment quitter l'agence ASK?
'Do you really want to leave agency ASK?' The verb meaning 'want' pairs naturally with the noun for 'the agency' in everyday conversation.
Un chasseur de têtes m'a contactée.
'A headhunter contacted me.' An objective explanation explaining external recruitment. This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past verb form for 'contacted'.
Noémie est très demandée pour son talent.

'Noemie is in high demand for her talent.' This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past verb form for 'sought-after'. This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past verb form for 'sought-after'.
Ce n'est peut-être pas le bon moment.
'This is perhaps not the right time.' A cautious opinion advising patient deliberation. The descriptive adjective for 'good' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Je vais réfléchir à toute cette situation.
'I am going to think about this whole situation.' A thoughtful concession promising careful reflection. Notice how 'am going' leads directly into the noun meaning 'situation'.
Mathias tient énormément à vous, Noémie.

'Mathias cares enormously about you, Noemie.' A profound revelation affirming deep professional loyalty. Catherine uses the polite 'you' form alongside 'cares' to keep a respectful professional tone. Now let's listen to Catherine, Mathias, and Noemie again at natural pace.

Moved by Catherine's compassionate insight and Mathias's quiet devotion, Noemie reconsiders her hasty departure from ASK. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'place' and 'table'. You'll catch them now. See you next time!
Bonne soirée!
